title: CYBERBRIEFING -- Sunday September 13, 2026: Microsoft record Patch Tuesday, Chrome seventh zero-day, ShieldCrash, TeamSystem breach, CRA enforcement begins
content_md:
CYBERBRIEFING -- Sunday September 13, 2026

IL PUNTO CYBER daily cybersecurity briefing, covering the last 24 hours.

Top story: Microsoft's September 2026 Patch Tuesday is the largest in its history: nearly 974 vulnerabilities patched in one release, almost double the previous record of July. Two zero-days are already actively exploited: one in the Windows ALPC component (CVE-2026-85880, enabling system-level privileges) and one in the Windows Update mechanism itself (CVE-2026-81963). Twenty of the patched vulnerabilities are wormable, meaning they could propagate between machines without user interaction, similar to WannaCry in 2017.

Additional items: Google patched Chrome's seventh zero-day of 2026 (CVE-2026-87491, a critical V8 JavaScript engine flaw already exploited in the wild, also affecting Edge, Brave, and Opera). A researcher disclosed ShieldCrash (CVE-2026-69414), a Windows privilege escalation bypassing a previous patch; Microsoft confirmed the issue but has not yet released a fix. Italian software provider TeamSystem suffered a breach of its Cloud Accounting service, exposing customer IBANs, names, emails, and phone numbers, raising risks of targeted phishing and invoice fraud. The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered enforcement on September 11, requiring manufacturers of digital products to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and serious incidents to national CSIRTs within 24 hours, with penalties up to 15 million euros or 2.5% of global revenue.
